config.title: Build Prometheus metrics endpoint

intro.title: Build Prometheus metrics endpoint
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple HTTP endpoint in Node.js that exposes Prometheus-style metrics. You will learn how to use the Node.js HTTP module to create a server that responds to requests with formatted metric data. The core concept involves handling HTTP requests and structuring responses with plain text content. By the end, you'll have a working endpoint that can be scraped by monitoring tools like Prometheus.
intro.usecase: Prometheus metrics endpoints are essential in production Node.js applications for monitoring system health and performance. Developers implement these endpoints to expose metrics like request rates, error counts, and response times, which are then visualized in dashboards like Grafana. This enables teams to detect anomalies, set up alerts, and make data-driven decisions to optimize application reliability and user experience.

objectives: Initialize a Node.js server with Express to handle HTTP requests
Configure a dedicated route for serving Prometheus metrics
Implement a metrics collection function to track HTTP request counts
Integrate the prom-client library to format metrics in Prometheus exposition format
Manipulate metric data to include labels for request methods and status codes
Render the formatted metrics through the configured endpoint
Control server startup and ensure the metrics endpoint is accessible

steps.instruction: Import the http module for creating a server and the os module for system metrics using Node.js's built-in require() syntax.
steps.hint: Use require('module_name') to import Node.js core modules. Both http and os are built-in modules, so you don't need to install them.

steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both the http and os modules using require() statements.

steps.title: Create function to collect system metrics
steps.instruction: Create a function named collectSystemMetrics that uses the os module to gather CPU and memory metrics and returns them as an object.
steps.hint: Use os.cpus() to get CPU information and os.totalmem() with os.freemem() for memory metrics. Return an object with properties like cpuCount, memoryTotal, and memoryFree.

successCriteria: The collectSystemMetrics function exists, uses os.cpus() and os.totalmem()/os.freemem(), and returns an object with at least cpuCount and memoryTotal properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it uses os.cpus() and os.totalmem()/os.freemem() and returns an object with CPU and memory properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The collectSystemMetrics function is missing or doesn't properly use the os module to gather CPU and memory metrics.

successCriteria: The formatMetrics function is defined with a parameter for the metrics object and returns a string in Prometheus exposition format.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
